subject: Composite discount proration & packaging mapping — redline questions
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2025-09-09T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Order form redline + question on composite discount application

Jordan —

Thanks for sending over the updated order form. We've gone through Exhibit B and the pricing schedule and pushed back a few redlines (attached: Acme_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf). Two closely related items came up during our procurement review that we need clarified before we can proceed to Countersign:

1) Composite discount stacking: the redline team is uncertain how the composite discount will apply when multiple SKU groups are purchased in the same billing period. The order form currently references a "composite slab" but doesn't define whether discounts prorate by revenue contribution or by unit share. Procurement needs an explicit formula and an example.

2) Packaging / unit-of-measure ambiguity: some of our SKUs (e.g., "Edge-Eval" and "Edge-Cache") are sold in packs of 5. The pricing schedule shows per-unit rates and a packaging column but the proration logic across pack vs unit isn't clear. If a customer consumes 12 units in a month (2 packs + 2 loose units), how does the discount apply? Do packs count as a single SKU for cap/floor purposes?

We attached our redline and flagged the clauses (see comments on Exhibit B, rows 14–18). Can you provide proposed contract language to address both items and an illustrative calculation for September under two scenarios (pack-heavy and unit-heavy)? Procurement is also pushing for monthly true-ups rather than quarterly — that's a negotiable point but they want to see the impact on caps/floors.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we were hoping to finalize before the end of next week.

Best,
Lena Park
Sourcing Manager, Acme Health
procurement@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Order form redline + question on composite discount application

Team / Lena —

Attaching a proposed markup for Exhibit B and a short matrix showing how the composite discount would compute under the two proration models (revenue-weighted vs unit-weighted). Key points in the proposed language (see proposed-exhibit-b-markup.docx):

- Define "SKU Group" and "Pack" explicitly. Example: "Pack(5)" means five (5) units. All references to units or usage shall be converted to 'units' using declared pack equivalence before applying any slab or composite discount.

- Composite discount formula (recommended default):
  CompositeDiscount = Sum_over_Groups( GroupRevenue / TotalRevenue * GroupDiscountRate )
  Where GroupRevenue = Sum(UnitPrice_i * UnitsConsumed_i) after pack normalization.

- Alternative (customer option): Unit-weighted proration where CompositeDiscount = Sum( Units_i / TotalUnits * GroupDiscountRate ). Use this only if the customer explicitly declares a pack-as-single-item commercial intent.

- Cap/floor interaction: add language that caps and floors apply to effective invoiced dollars after composite discount has been applied, and that the cap is assessed at the billing-period level (monthly or quarterly as elected).

- Example included: Scenario A (pack-heavy month) and Scenario B (unit-heavy month), showing step-by-step calculations and resulting effective per-unit price. We also included a worked sensitivity on the cap: what the customer would pay if their true-up moves them above the ceiling.

A couple of open operational questions for Acme to confirm so we can finalize language:
  1) Do you want packs treated as indivisible commercial SKUs for any reporting/SLAs? (That affects how we show usage on the invoice.)
  2) If you elect monthly true-up, do you want us to bill provisional amounts during the month and true-up at month-end, or only invoice post-monthly reconciliation? (Operational impact on cashflow and estimated billing.)

I'll run the doc past legal for a narrow redline (we kept it prescriptive to avoid wiggle room). Jordan — if you want, I can produce a version with quarterly-only language as an alternate.

Marissa Cole
Pricing & Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

Jordan / Marissa —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the example matrix; that helped a lot. A few follow-ups from procurement after reviewing the proposed language and the worked examples:

- The revenue-weighted default looks reasonable, but procurement asks that the contract include a one-sentence example inside Exhibit B (not just the SOW) so the calculation is binding. Can you insert the small worked example from your matrix into Exhibit B itself?

- For packs: Acme will accept pack normalization for discount calculations but requests that packs remain visible on the invoice line item (we need packs for our internal inventory reconciliation). So we'd like the clause to say: "Pack normalization is used for discount and cap/floor computation; invoices will display both pack and normalized unit counts."

- Monthly true-up preference: procurement wants monthly true-ups with provisional invoicing (i.e., invoice estimated amounts weekly, true-up at month-end). They asked us to confirm any unit rounding rules in that flow (e.g., do provisional invoices round up to the nearest pack?).

If you can incorporate: (a) the one-sentence example in Exhibit B; (b) the invoice visibility sentence; and (c) explicit rounding rules for provisional invoices, we can move this to Legal for countersign.

I'll leave the formal redline comments in the attached PDF (we highlighted the exact insertion points). If you want to discuss live, I can do 10–10:30am PT tomorrow.

Best,
Lena
